195878681_8363d433.text: Intermingled within the LH are neurons defined by neurotransmitter markers such as vesicular GABA transporter (SLC32A1 commonly known as VGAT) (Stuber et al., 2016)(Karnani et al., 2013)(Jennings et al., 2013) and vesicular glutamate transporter 2 (SLC17A6 commonly known as VGLUT2) (Stuber et al., 2016)(Jennings et al., 2013)(Ziegler et al., 2002). Moreover, many of these neurons can be identified by expression of neuropeptides, including hypocretin (orexin; HCRT), melanin-concentrating hormone (MCH), neurotensin (NTS), and galanin (GAL) as well as receptors such as leptin receptor (LEPR) [10](Cason et al., 2010)(Griffond et al., 2009)(Leinninger et al., 2009)(Laque et al., 2013)(Goforth et al., 2014)(Allen et al., 1995).

Moreover, many of these neurons can be identified by expression of neuropeptides, including hypocretin (orexin; HCRT), melanin-concentrating hormone (MCH), neurotensin (NTS), and galanin (GAL) as well as receptors such as leptin receptor (LEPR) [10](Cason et al., 2010)(Griffond et al., 2009)(Leinninger et al., 2009)(Laque et al., 2013)(Goforth et al., 2014)(Allen et al., 1995). Due to this heterogeneity, it is not surprising that LH electrical stimulation evokes a variety of behavioral effects including feeding, grooming, gnawing, sexual behavior, motivation, and reinforcement [17](Singh et al., 1996)(Glickman et al., 1967).
